question:
The selling prices of articles A and B are the same. A is sold at a profit of 28 percent and B is sold at a loss of 24 percent. If the total selling price of both articles is ₹48640, then what is the cost price of A and B, respectively?

(CGL MAINS 2021)
solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. ₹19000, ₹32000.

+28% = +\(\frac{7}{25}\)
– 24% = -\(\frac{6}{25}\)
                 A                            B

Total SP = 608 + 608 = 1216 
1216 unit → ×40 → ₹48640 
∴ CP(A) = 25 × 19 × 40 = ₹19000 
CP(B) = 25 × 32 × 40 = ₹32000
question_hi:
वस्तुओं A तथा B के विक्रय मूल्य समान हैं। A को 28 प्रतिशत के लाभ पर बेचा जाता है। तथा B को 24 प्रतिशत की हानि पर बेचा जाता है। यदि दोनों वस्तुओं का कुल विक्रय मूल्य ₹48640 हो, तो A तथा B का क्रय मूल्य क्या है? 

(CGL MAINS 2021)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 अर्थात ₹19000, ₹32000 है।

+28% = +\(\frac{7}{25}\)
– 24% = -\(\frac{6}{25}\)

                               A                            B 

कुल विक्रय मूल्य = 608 + 608 = 1216
1216 इकाई → ×40 → ₹48640
∴ क्रय मूल्य (A) = 25 × 19 × 40 = ₹19000
क्रय मूल्य (B) = 25 × 32 × 40 = ₹32000

question:
Last year Neil bought two watches. This year he sold them for 15,000 each. On one, he made a 25% profit and on the other, he had a x% loss. If his net loss is ₹2000, then find the value of x?

(SSC GD 2024)
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 25.

              I           :        II
SP    15000      :  15000
CP1  12000

CP₁ ⇒ 15000 × \(\frac{100}{125}\) = 12000

His total loss = ₹2000 
∴ CP of both = 15000 × 2 + 2000  = ₹32000

∴ CP of 2nd watch = 32000 - 12000 = ₹20000
Loss on 2nd (x) = 20000 – 15000 = ₹5000 
loss% = \(\frac{5000}{20000}\) × 100 = 25%
question_hi:
पिछले साल नील ने दो घड़ियाँ खरीदीं। इस साल उसने इन्हें 15-15 हजार रुपये में बेच दिया। एक पर उसे 25% का लाभ हुआ और दूसरी पर उसे x% हानि हुई। यदि उसकी कुल हानि ₹2000 है, तो x का मान ज्ञात कीजिये।

(SSC GD 2024)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 अर्थात 25 है।

                         I                   II
विक्रय मूल्य     15000         15000
क्रय मूल्य1       12000

क्रय मूल्य1 ⇒ 15000 × \(\frac{100}{125}\)= 12000

उसकी कुल हानि = ₹2000
∴ दोनों का क्रय मूल्य = 15000 × 2 + 2000 = ₹32000

∴ दूसरी घड़ी का क्रय मूल्य = 32000 - 12000 = ₹20000
दूसरी पर हानि (x) = 20000 – 15000 = ₹5000
हानि% = \(\frac{5000}{20000}\)× 100 = 25%

question:
A seller sold 19 cookies for ₹95 instead of 20 cookies in one kg, cheating a customer. What is the gain (in ₹) if the seller bought the cookies for ₹76?

(CGL 2024 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 22.8.

Cost price per cookie = 76/20 = ₹3.80 

Selling price per cookie = 95/19 = ₹5

Profit per cookie= 5 - 3.80 = ₹1.20

Total profit = 1.2 × 19 = ₹22.8

(CGL 2024 Pre)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 अर्थात 22.8 है।

प्रति कुकी लागत मूल्य = 76/20 = ₹3.80

प्रति कुकी विक्रय मूल्य = 95/19 = ₹5

प्रति कुकी लाभ = 5 - 3.80 = ₹1.20

कुल लाभ = 1.2 × 19 = ₹22.8

question:
A shopkeeper has a fault of 100 gm in a 3 kg weight. He sold 3 kg of potatoes to Charu using the same faulty weight for ₹46. The cost price of the potatoes for the seller was ₹12 per kg. How much profit (in ₹) did he earn on the potatoes?

(CGL 2024 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. ₹11.6.

Selling price per kg = \(\frac{46}{2.9}\) = \(\frac{460}{29}\) Rs/kg

Profit per kg = \(\frac{460}{29}\) – 12 = \(460-348\over29\) = ₹\(\frac{112}{29}\)

∴ Total profit on 3 kg = \(\frac{112}{29}\) × 3 = ₹11.586 = ₹11.6
question_hi:
एक दुकानदार के 3 किलो के बाट में 100 ग्राम की खराबी है। उसने उसी खराब बाट का इस्तेमाल करके चारू को ₹46 में 3 किलो आलू बेचे। विक्रेता के लिए आलू का क्रय मूल्य ₹12 प्रति किलो था। आलू पर उसे कितना लाभ (₹ में) हुआ?

(CGL 2024 Pre)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 अर्थात ₹11.6 है।

विक्रय मूल्य प्रति किलोग्राम = \(\frac{46}{2.9}\) = \(\frac{460}{29}\) रुपये/किग्रा

प्रति किलोग्राम लाभ = \(\frac{460}{29}\)– 12 = \(460-348\over29\) = ₹\(\frac{112}{29}\)

∴ 3 किग्रा पर कुल लाभ = \(\frac{112}{29}\)× 3 = ₹11.586 = ₹11.6

question:

question:
Some fruits are bought at 15 for ₹140, and an equal number of fruits at 10 for ₹120. If all the fruits are sold at ₹132 per dozen, then what is the profit percentage in the entire transaction?

(CGL 2020 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 3\(\frac{1}{8}\)%.

Case 1: 30 fruits at 15 for ₹140

15 fruits = ₹140

30 fruits = ₹140 × 2 = ₹280

Case 2: 30 fruits at 10 for ₹120

10 fruits = ₹120

30 fruits = ₹120 × 3 = ₹360

Total Cost Price (CP) = ₹280 + ₹360 = ₹640

Selling rate = ₹132 per dozen

⇒ 60 fruits = 5 dozens

⇒ SP = 5 × ₹132 = ₹660

Profit = SP - CP

⇒ 660 - 640 = 20

Profit% = (20/640) × 100 = 3.125% or 3\(\frac{1}{8}\)%
question_hi:
कुछ फल 15 रुपये में 140 रुपये में खरीदे जाते हैं, और समान संख्या में फल 10 रुपये में 120 रुपये में खरीदे जाते हैं। यदि सभी फल 132 रुपये प्रति दर्जन की दर से बेचे जाते हैं, तो पूरे लेन-देन में लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?

(CGL 2020 Pre)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 यानी 3\(\frac{1}{8}\)% है।

केस 1: 30 फल 15 के हिसाब से ₹140

15 फल = ₹140

30 फल = ₹140 × 2 = ₹280

केस 2: 30 फल 10 के हिसाब से ₹120

10 फल = ₹120

30 फल = ₹120 × 3 = ₹360

कुल लागत मूल्य (CP) = ₹280 + ₹360 = ₹640

बिक्री दर = ₹132 प्रति दर्जन

⇒ 60 फल = 5 दर्जन

⇒ विक्रय मूल्य = 5 × ₹132 = ₹660

लाभ = विक्रय मूल्य - क्रय मूल्य 

⇒ 660 - 640 = 20

लाभ% = (20/640) × 100 = 3.125% या 3\(\frac{1}{8}\)%

question:
A fruit merchant bought some bananas. One-fifth of them got rotten and were thrown away. He sold two-fifths of the bananas at 15% profit and the remaining bananas at 10% profit. Find his overall loss or profit percent.

(CGL 2020 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. Loss 10.4%.

1/5 of 100 = 20 bananas (thrown away) 

Left = 80

Rest 48 bananas sold at 10% profit 

SP of 48 bananas = ₹52.8 

Total CP = ₹100

Loss% = \((100-89.6)\times100\over100\) = 10.4%

100 का 1/5 = 20 केले (फेंक दिए गए)

शेष = 80

कुल विक्रय मूल्य = 52.8 + 36.8 = ₹89.6

हानि%= \((100-89.6)\times100\over100\) = 10.4%

question:
A shopkeeper bought a certain number of apples for ₹3,600. He sold one-fifth of them at a loss of 10%, one-fourth of the remaining apples at a loss of 5%, and two-thirds of the rest at a profit of 15%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the remaining apples to earn a profit of 27% overall?

(CGL 2023 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 1,584.

Let he bought 3600 apples for ₹3600

SP for overall 27% Profit = 3600 \(\times\frac{127}{100}\) = ₹4572

SP of 1/5 apples = \(\frac{1}{5}\times\ 3600\ \times\frac{9}{10}\) = ₹648 

SP of remaining apples = \(\frac{4}{5}\times\ 3600\ \times\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{19}{20}\) = 684 

SP of remaining apples = \(\frac{4}{5}\times\ 3600\ \times\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{23}{20}\)= ₹1656

∴ Remaining apples should be sold = 4572 – 648 – 684 – 1656 = ₹1584

question:
Ramesh purchased 130 books at the rate of ₹200 each and sold half of them at the rate of ₹300 each, one-fifth of them at the rate of ₹350 each, and the rest at the cost price. Find his profit percentage.

(CGL 2024 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 40%.

SP = 65 × 300 + 26 × 350 + 39 × 200

⇒ 19500 + 9100 + 7800  = ₹36400

Profit = 36400 – 130 × 200 

⇒ 36400 – ₹26000 = ₹10400 

Profit% = \(\frac{10400}{26000}\)× 100% = 40%

question:
